title: AWS Lambda Web Function behind Amazon CloudFront with Origin Access Control
description: Web app hosting on AWS Lambda: serve a Lambda Web Function only through a CloudFront distribution: an IamAuth endpoint, an OAC that signs origin requests, and a resource policy that trusts one distribution.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern deploys a plain Node.js HTTP server as an AWS Lambda Web Function and puts an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of it. The function's endpoint uses the IamAuth authentication type, so Lambda accepts only requests signed with AWS Signature Version 4 and returns 403 to everything else before your code runs.

CloudFront signs each origin request through an Origin Access Control of type lambda with SigningBehavior: always-amz-auth. A resource policy on the function allows lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint for the CloudFront service principal only when AWS:SourceArn matches your distribution, so a different distribution using the same origin is also denied.

After validating the signature, Lambda removes the Authorization header it used and forwards the viewer's own headers, so the application has no authentication code of its own and existing sign-in flows keep working. The app returns Cache-Control headers that CloudFront honours, which the pattern uses to show edge caching.
With CloudFront in front you can add a custom domain, AWS WAF, compression and caching to a Web Function without changing the application.

bullets.text: Lambda Web Function endpoint access control
Restricting access to an origin with CloudFront Origin Access Control

text: Set your Region, export AWS_REGION=us-east-1, then run ./deploy.sh.

The script deploys the Web Function with aws lambda-web deploy --auth-type IamAuth, creates the OAC, a cache policy that forwards the viewer's Authorization header, and the distribution, attaches the resource policy and waits for the distribution to deploy.
See the GitHub repo for detailed testing instructions.
Disable and delete the CloudFront distribution, then delete the cache policy and the OAC, then aws lambda-web delete-web-function --function-name lambda-web-cloudfront-oac.
See the GitHub repo for removing the execution role and log groups.
